new_statements.quote: The boundaries of this zone are in general well defined in spite of an occasional divergence from smooth homogeniety. new_statements.second_reader_evidence: archive.org metadata downloaded: micro_IA41153350_0260 is an open ERIC microfiche dated 1964-05 whose catalogue title reads 'LANGUAGES OF THE WORLD--AFRICAN FASCICLE THREE', but the scanned running head in the saved extract is 'Anthropological Linguistics, Vol. 6, No. 5' p. 138 = A's citation (AL 6(5)). Quote found in the mirror extract at the Zone M paragraph: scanned has 'fro m smooth homogeniety' and a stray quote mark, and A's ellipsis skips the (10) Fipa-Mambwe list before '(20) Nyika-Safwa Group (21) Wanda (Iciwanda, Wandia), 6,000 speakers (1934)'; otherwise verbatim. Reading/statement_type agree as a description of the text, but identity_ok=false: the tone sentence is a Zone M gener…
new_statements.relation_note: Zone M: 5- or 7-vowel systems; grammatical (tense-distinguishing) tone general except M.60; Nyakyusa toneless.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Zone M languages (which include M.21 Wanda) use tone grammatically - tone is often the sole marker distinguishing tenses - except the Lenje-Tonga group; Nyakyusa alone is said to use no tone. Nothing on word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Group M.60 (Lenje-Tonga) excluded from the tense-tone remark; Nyakyusa M.31 'makes no use of tone at all'.
new_statements.identity_note: Zone-level generalization for Guthrie's Zone M, which lists '(21) Wanda (Iciwanda, Wandia), 6,000 speakers (1934)' in the (20) Nyika-Safwa group; nothing is said about Wanda individually. Secondhand from Guthrie 1948 The Classification of the Bantu Languages. | M 21 Wanda listed in group X with iwa, namwanga, mambwe, lungu, fipa, lambya, tambo, nyiha, malela, safwa, ndali, nyakyusa = Iciwanda of Mbozi/Sumbawanga (wand1264); no cross in Tableau 1 = poorly documented [name in source: wanda (M 21) (groupe X Corridor); pages 71 (Tableau 1), 424-425 (2.3.2), 483 (3.5.2c, citing Guthrie 1948: 58)]

new_statements.quote: 2.3.2 Un cas intéressant est présenté par le safwa et, sans doute, plusieurs autres langues voisines du groupe X (nyiha, malela, lambya, wanda, etc.). Les thèmes nominaux (quelle que soit leur longueur) se divisent en trois schèmes, dont l'un - accent sur la pénultième - ne comprend qu'un très petit nombre de thèmes (...). L'immense majorité des nominaux se présente, soit avec un accent sur l'antépénultième (l'accent par défaut), soit sur l'augment, si celui-ci est présent, autrement sur la finale. [p. 483:] Guthrie signale (1948, p.58) que certaines langues du sud de la Tanzanie (sa zone M), bien que possédant opposition de longueur et prosodèmes distinctifs, n'en allongent pas moins légèrement une syllabe pénultième longue; il cite les exemples suivants pour le wanda
new_statements.translation: 2.3.2 An interesting case is presented by Safwa and, no doubt, several other neighbouring languages of group X (Nyiha, Malila, Lambya, Wanda, etc.). Noun stems (of whatever length) divide into three schemes, one of which - accent on the penultimate - contains only a very small number of stems (...). The vast majority of nominals have either an accent on the antepenultimate (the default accent) or on the augment if present, otherwise on the final. [p. 483:] Guthrie (1948:58) notes that some languages of southern Tanzania (his zone M), although possessing a length opposition and distinctive prosodemes, nonetheless slightly lengthen a long penultimate syllable; he cites the following examples for Wanda ...
new_statements.citation: Philippson, Gérard. 1991. Tons et accent dans les langues bantu d'Afrique orientale : étude comparative typologique et diachronique. Thèse de doctorat d'État, Université Paris V René Descartes (theses.fr 1992PA05H011). DDL Lyon PDF edition, 542 pp.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. Philippson's accent-scheme description (pp.424-425) is of Safwa (Voorhoeve 1973), extended 'sans doute' to 'plusieurs autres langues voisines du groupe X (nyiha, malela, lambya, wanda, etc.)'; his Tableau 1 (mirror the text) lists 'wanda (M 21)' with no data mark (+/++), i.e. he had no Wanda tonal data of his own. The only Wanda-specific content is secondhand from Guthrie 1948:58 (distinctive prosodemes, length opposition, slight penult lengthening). 'pitch accent' is therefore a conjecture; record as tonal per Guthrie (secondhand), type undetermined. | checker: Philippson 1991 these d'Etat: PDF + extracted text held in the mirror (nyat1246/, 1.9 MB,…
new_statements.relation_note: Hedged ('sans doute'): Wanda probably shares the Safwa restricted-tone ('accent') system with three lexical noun schemes - default accent on the antepenultimate, a small class with penultimate accent, and a class accented on the augment (or, without augment, on the final); separately quotes Guthrie 1948:58 that Wanda, a zone-M language with length opposition and distinctive prosodemes, slightly lengthens a long penultimate.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Probably a Safwa-type restricted tone/accent system: lexical accent classes (antepenult default; few penult; augment/final); Guthrie's Wanda forms carry tone marks and vowel length.
new_statements.exceptions: statement explicitly hedged ('sans doute'); Philippson adds that in his own sparse data for the region he did not note Guthrie's penultimate lengthening

sources.citation: Karels, Jacob. 2014. Relative Constructions in Nyiha: An Investigation of the Syntax, Semantics and Activation Status of Information in Relative Constructions in Nyiha, a Bantu Language of Southwestern Tanzania (M23). SIL Electronic Working Papers 2014-008. SIL International. 52 pp.
sources.note: Nothing about Wanda (wbh) prosody. The paper is a syntax/discourse study of Mbozi Nyiha (M23) relative clauses; its only tone remarks are Nyiha-internal (relative pronoun with long vowel and high falling tone vs. morphologically similar low-toned copula, sec. 2.2.2.1; a passing note that contour tones may mark the right edge of the RC in Wandya per Mtenje 2011 and Bemba). 'Wanda' appears only in the Ethnologue M20 member list (p. 1), in footnote 2 (which argues that Mtenje 2011's Ciwandya of Malawi is Wandya, a Zambian Nyiha dialect, and not Wanda M21, citing Walsh and Swilla 2000:12), and in…

sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project, 'Wanda' (lang/5076), snapshot 2025-06-09 via the Internet Archive
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Resolves 'Mitterhofer 2014' as 'Personal Communication on Wanda' (Bernadette Mitterhofer, SIL, 2014): vitality, location (Kamsamba ward, Momba DC; Kipeta ward, Sumbawanga), orthography 'None'. Quotes Walsh & Swilla 2001: 'Very little has been written about the Wanda people and their language, iciwanda.'

sources.citation: Lindfors, Anna-Lena, Mark Woodward & Louise Nagler. 2009. A sociolinguistic survey of Sichela speech community. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-014. Dallas: SIL International. 20 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sichela is treated as a dialect of Wanda (86% probable cognates with the SIL Wanda wordlist, p. 16-17). The wordlist was written 'in broad phonetic transcription using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA). Tone was not noted.' (p. 9, sec. 3.4). Sec. 3.5 lists only phonological correspondences used for cognate counting (spirantization, metathesis, extra syllables). No word on stress or accent. Cites Daggett et al. 1999 as the only prior document on the Wanda.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919/1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vols. 1-2. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.note: Wanda appears only as 'ICI-WANDA', a 'northern dialect' of Isi-nyixa (no. 49), vol. 2 p. 60 with footnote 'Quite distinct from the Ici-wandia language (No. 50) farther to the south-east'. No stress remark for Wanda/Nyixa. The footnote 'The accent, it might be mentioned, is always on the penultimate, except where otherwise indicated' (vol. 2, verb paradigmata, p. ~497) is a general note on the sample paradigms (Runyoro etc.), not about Wanda. Vol. 1 has only scattered Ci-wanda vocabulary items.

sources.citation: Hamberger, Alois. 1909. Religiöse Überlieferungen und Gebräuche der Landschaft Mkulwe (Deutsch-Ostafrika). Anthropos 4: 295-317 (with Nachtrag in Anthropos 5, 1910).
sources.note: Only a segmental alphabet key (p. 297-298: 'will ich erst kurz das angewandte Alphabet erläutern: a, b, c, d, e, f, g, ng, h, i, j, k, l, m, n, o, p, r, s, sh, t, u, v, w, y, z' with values of c, e, ng, j, sh, w, z); no accent, length or tone marks and no remark on Betonung/Ton anywhere in the article (searched Betonung, Akzent, Ton, Silbe, betont). About 20 pages of interlinear texts (creation, origin of death, prayers, divination formulas) usable as early Wanda-area text material.
